back: A model showing how birth rates, death rates and population change in five stages as a country develops.
1: high birth and death rates, low growth. 2: death rate falls rapidly, birth rate high, rapid growth.
3: birth rate falls, growth slows. 4: both low, stable. 5: births below deaths, decline.
Based on Europe; ignores migration, disease (HIV/AIDS), war, policy and culture; no time scale; LIC transition faster.
About 1 billion (1800), 3 billion (1960), 6 billion (1999), 7 billion (2011), 8 billion (2022) - UN estimates.
Stage 3: falling birth rate, low death rate; HIV and AIDS raised deaths in the 1990s-2000s; emigration not in model.
Family planning, women's education and work, urbanisation, lower infant mortality, later marriage, cost of children.
Pressure on services, jobs, land and housing; environmental degradation; but a large future workforce and market.
Labour shortage, ageing, pension costs, closing schools; but less pressure on resources and land.
